E1.evidence: Issue #848 gives a reproducer ("Clone [nan_publisher](https://github.com/jacobperron/nan_publisher) ... ros2 run nan_publisher nan_publisher ... ros2 topic echo /nan") and the error: "make_tuple(): unable to convert argument of type 'object' to Python object". Maintainer (clalancette): "https://github.com/ros2/rosidl_python/pull/167 can fix this problem." / "Yes, good call.  I'm actually going to close this one as a duplicate, since it is already fixed in Rolling". https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/issues/848

units_identified: rclpy subscriber (ros2 topic echo) with the rosidl_generator_py-generated Python message binding
nan_publisher (C++ publisher of NaN values on /nan)
E2.evidence: The crash is in the subscriber's own conversion logic and happens for any correct publisher that sends a NaN, which is a legitimate IEEE/ROS float value. The generated Python setter asserted a range that NaN can never satisfy; rosidl_python PR #167 ('Allow NaN values to pass floating point bounds check.') changes the generated check from "-            assert value >= -@(bound) and value <= @(bound), \" to "+            assert not (value < -@(bound) or value > @(bound)) or math.isinf(value), \". rosidl_python #162 states the expected behavior: "The NaN value should be converted to a NaN in python." and notes "The [BatteryState] message, for example, uses NaNs to flag values that are not measured." rclpy then passes the failed conversion result on unchecked: "pytaken_msg = convert_to_py(taken_msg.get(), pymsg_type);" followed by "return py::make_tuple(pytaken_msg, ..." (subscription.cpp at 77949d2c). The NaN crossing the boundary is not a wrong value; the defect is the binding's rejection of a valid value plus rclpy's unchecked error path, both inside the subscribing process.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the C++ nan_publisher publishes on /nan and the rclpy-based ros2 topic echo takes the message.

E4.evidence: Observed failure: "The subscriber crashes with the following message: make_tuple(): unable to convert argument of type 'object' to Python object".

ineligible_reason: internal: the rosidl_generator_py-generated Python message binding rejects NaN (and inf) with a bounds assertion, and rclpy's take path does not check the failed conversion; the failure occurs with any correct publisher of NaN, and the value crossing the boundary is valid.
notes: Other compositions in the thread: (1) the original discovery, a stereo_image_proc test where an unpopulated CameraInfo P matrix caused a division by zero ("A division by zero is happening here ... causing a `-nan` getting set in the ROS message") and the Python test subscriber crashed; image_pipeline PR #710 / commits 7d06a907, 78fe7e30, bc8c41be, d5e295e8 ('Populate CameraInfo camera matrix in test fixture') work around it in the test fixture, not in the interface. (2) tier4/pilot_auto_tier4_api PR #56 ('fix: rtc distance') works around the same rclpy/rosidl_python behavior on the publisher side by replacing non-finite CooperateStatus.distance with -100000.0 ("If subscribing NaN value on humble rclpy(version 3.3.4), rclpy is broken."). image_pipeline PR #699 ('[rolling] Fix image saver bug and time-based image saving') is unrelated to this defect. Alternative reading considered: rosidl_python #169 frames it as a C++/Python inconsistency after rosidl_python #128 introduced the bounds check ("our c++ code is still able to serialize using `std::numeric_limits<T>::infinity` but the python code is not able to do so"), which could be treated as a value-domain or UPGRADE mismatch between language bindings; it was not, because NaN/inf are valid values for the declared float types and the maintainers fixed the Python check itself. Reporter environment: Ubuntu 20.04, rclpy 77949d2c, rmw_fastrtps_cpp and rmw_cyclonedds. Issue closed 2022-11-07 as a duplicate (state_reason not_planned); rosidl_python PR #167 merged into rolling 2022-08-22 as 52e099ef.
